title: Build n objects from a factory Supplier

blocks.text: A `Supplier` is a natural factory: `ArrayList::new` is a `Supplier<List<String>>` that makes a **new** list every time it is asked. `Stream.generate(supplier)` asks it again and again, forever, so it must always be paired with `limit(n)`.
Write `Factory.createN(int n, Supplier<T> factory)`, returning a list of `n` objects made by `factory`. The page's tool is `Stream.generate` with `limit`.
A negative `n` throws `IllegalArgumentException("n must not be negative: " + n)`. Mind how many times the factory is asked, including when the answer is empty.

cases.says: The list holds n objects, each made by the factory.
The factory is asked once per element, so no two elements are the same object.
For n = 0 the list is empty and the factory is never called.
A negative n is rejected with a message that names it.

concepts: A factory Supplier such as ArrayList::new makes a new object on every call, so each element is its own.
Stream.generate is infinite, so it is always paired with limit or another short-circuiting step.
